app.name: On the record
app.caveat: Hand-written examples, not a live audit. Volumes are plausible orders of magnitude rather than observed counts. What is held varies by country, handset, and settings. See Method for how the corpus is built.

inferred.label: Inferred
inferred.gloss: A model produced it. You never gave it.

relational.label: Relational
relational.gloss: It is about other people too.

documented.label: Documented
documented.gloss: Supported by a regulator, a court, or the holder's own disclosure.

reported.label: Reported
reported.gloss: Supported by credible journalism or research.

modelled.label: Modelled
modelled.gloss: No public source; asserted from how these systems are known to work.

method.title: Method
method.corpusBody: Each record names a datum, who holds it, how it is generated, and under what conditions it applies. Records are hand-written and reviewed against regulatory findings, litigation, journalism, academic research, official policy guidance, and vendors' own documentation before anything is marked documented or reported.
method.confidenceDocumented: Documented — a regulator, a court, or the holder itself has disclosed this in writing.
method.confidenceReported: Reported — credible journalism or peer-reviewed research has described this.
method.confidenceModelled: Modelled — no public source exists; the record describes how this class of system is known to work. Most inferences fall here, because inference is what firms disclose least.
method.limitsBody: This is not a live audit of any named company, and it does not know what any specific holder does with any specific person's data today. Practices change, vary by jurisdiction, and are frequently undisclosed by design. Treat every count as an illustrative order of magnitude, not a measurement.
method.inferenceHeading: Why inference is the least documentable part
method.inferenceBody: Emitted records usually leave some trace the person can point to. Inferences are computed internally, rarely disclosed, and almost never shown to the person they describe — so the tier that most needs scrutiny is structurally the one with the least public evidence. That asymmetry is itself part of the argument this app is making, not a gap to be apologetic about.
